# Why MgCl₂ and Not MgCl?

<!-- STEP id="mgcl" -->
## Magnesium and Chlorine

Magnesium is 2,8,2, so it tends to lose 2 electrons and become Mg²⁺. A chlorine atom gains only 1 electron, so one chlorine cannot take both. It takes two chlorine atoms, which gives the formula MgCl₂. The charges add up to zero: +2, −1 and −1.

<!-- STEP id="sulfide" -->
## Sodium and Sulfur

Sulfur is 2,8,6, so it tends to gain 2 electrons and become S²⁻. A sodium atom loses only 1 electron, so it takes two sodium atoms to supply them. That gives Na₂S, and the charges again add up to zero: +1, +1 and −2.

<!-- STEP id="takeaway" -->
## Plus and Minus Add Up to Zero

Every electron that one atom loses, another atom gains, so nothing is left over.

**The charges in an ionic compound always add up to zero, and this sets the formula.**
